common_name: Falcon Southern Highbush Blueberry (Jumbo Very-Low-Chill Florida Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant or container-grown bushes into acidic, pine-bark-amended beds during winter; a very-low-chill University of Florida release suited to the mildest Gulf Coast winters, grown under the evergreen (non-defoliating) production system used for early-market southern highbush blueberries.

directions: Falcon is a 2023 University of Florida southern highbush release bred for jumbo-sized, sweet-flavored berries that ripen early in the season, giving Deep South growers an entry into the earliest and most profitable picking window. It performs best under the evergreen production system common to Florida's low-chill growing regions, where leaves are retained through winter rather than defoliated by cold. Plant in raised, sulfur-acidified beds with excellent drainage, and pair with a second early-season southern highbush cultivar to improve pollination and berry size.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Southern Highbush Blueberry Cultivars (EDIS HS1245)
University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences

common_name: Albus Southern Highbush Blueberry (Firm Extended-Harvest Low-Chill Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant during winter dormancy into very acidic (pH 4.5-5.5), well-drained soil amended with pine bark; low chill requirement, grown under the evergreen production system, holding fruit quality from early harvest through the end of the southern highbush season.

directions: Albus is a 2022 University of Florida southern highbush release notable for holding firm fruit quality from the start of harvest all the way through the end of the picking season, rather than declining as many cultivars do late in the cycle. Its low chill requirement fits it for the mildest Gulf Coast winters, and it is typically grown under the evergreen (leaf-retaining) production system. Plant in raised, well-drained acidic beds and pair with another low-chill southern highbush cultivar for cross-pollination and fuller berry set.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Southern Highbush Blueberry Cultivars (EDIS HS1245)
University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences

common_name: Wayne Southern Highbush Blueberry (Firm Early-Maturing North-Central Florida Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant or container-grown bushes into acidic, pine-bark-amended raised beds in winter; carries a medium-to-high chill requirement for a southern highbush, better suited to north-central Florida and similar Gulf Coast zones than the mildest coastal strip.

directions: Wayne is a 2017 University of Florida southern highbush release bred for consistent early maturity and firmer fruit than the older standard Jewel, making it a good hand-harvest option for north-central Florida and comparable Gulf Coast growing areas. Its chill requirement runs higher than many UF releases, so it is best matched to sites with cooler winters within the region rather than the mildest coastal strip. Plant in sulfur-acidified, well-drained beds and provide a second early-season southern highbush cultivar nearby to improve pollination. Renewal-prune out the oldest canes each winter to keep the bush productive.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Southern Highbush Blueberry Cultivars (EDIS HS1245)
University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences

common_name: Avanti Southern Highbush Blueberry (Firm Very-Low-Chill Small-Scar Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant during winter dormancy into very acidic (pH 4.5-5.5), well-drained soil amended with pine bark; very low chill requirement, grown under the evergreen production system typical of the mildest Deep South and peninsular Florida blueberry regions.

directions: Avanti is a 2015 University of Florida southern highbush release valued for firm, high-quality fruit with a small, dry picking scar that resists juice leakage after harvest. Its very low chill requirement makes it one of the better choices for the warmest Gulf Coast winters, though the bush can be more susceptible to Botrytis fruit rot in wet, humid conditions, so good air circulation and a preventive fungicide program during bloom are worthwhile. Plant in raised, sulfur-amended beds with excellent drainage and pair with another very-low-chill cultivar for fuller pollination.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Southern Highbush Blueberry Cultivars (EDIS HS1245)
University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences

common_name: Flicker Southern Highbush Blueberry (Early-Season Low-Chill Florida Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant or container-grown bushes into acidic, pine-bark-amended raised beds in winter; low chill requirement suited to Gulf Coast winters, one of a set of bird-named early-harvest University of Florida southern highbush releases.

directions: Flicker is a 2009 University of Florida southern highbush release bred for early-season harvest potential in low-chill climates, part of the same UF breeding cycle that produced Kestrel, Chickadee, and Meadowlark. Growers should watch for anthracnose fruit rot in wet spring weather, as this cultivar can be more prone to the disease than some newer releases, so a preventive fungicide program through bloom and fruit set is recommended. Plant in raised, sulfur-acidified beds with excellent drainage, and provide a second early-blooming southern highbush cultivar nearby to improve pollination.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Southern Highbush Blueberry Cultivars (EDIS HS1245)
University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences

common_name: Florida Rose Rabbiteye Blueberry (Pink-Fruited Novelty Low-Chill Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant or container-grown bushes into acidic, well-drained soil amended with pine bark during winter dormancy; carries a very low chill requirement of roughly 300 hours, among the lowest of any named rabbiteye, well matched to Gulf Coast winters.

directions: Florida Rose is a University of Florida rabbiteye selection bred by Paul Lyrene and notable for large, sweet, low-acid berries that stay pink on the sun-exposed side and pale on the shaded side at full ripeness, rather than the typical blue-black rabbiteye color. Its roughly 300-hour chill requirement is unusually low for a rabbiteye cultivar, letting it fruit reliably in the mildest Deep South gardens where standard rabbiteyes may underperform. As with all rabbiteye blueberries, it is not self-fertile and needs a different rabbiteye cultivar blooming at the same time for good pollination and full-sized berries.
sources: University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences
US Plant Patent USPP14,485

planting.note: Plant year-round from containers in mild Gulf Coast winters, or during dormancy elsewhere, into acidic, well-drained potting mix or raised beds; selected from a naturally occurring Florida hybrid and comfortable with warm, low-chill winters.

directions: Blueberry Buckle traces back to a chance seedling found near Hawthorne, Florida, apparently a natural cross between native shiny blueberry (Vaccinium myrsinites) and highbush blueberry, patented as Corablue and sold under the Bushel and Berry brand. It forms a compact, rounded shrub with small, glossy, semi-evergreen leaves that give it ornamental value beyond its fruit, making it a good fit for patio containers as well as garden beds. It is self-fertile and will set some fruit alone, but yields and berry size improve noticeably with a compatible blueberry cultivar planted nearby for cross-pollination.
sources: US Plant Patent USPP22,521
Fall Creek Farm and Nursery — Bushel and Berry Collection

common_name: BerryBux Dwarf Blueberry (Boxwood-Like Self-Pollinating Container Blueberry, 'ZF08-095')

planting.note: Plant year-round from containers in mild Gulf Coast winters, or during dormancy elsewhere, into acidic, well-drained potting mix or raised beds; moderate-to-low chill requirement in the low hundreds of hours, comfortable for most Gulf Coast gardens.

directions: BerryBux is a patented dwarf blueberry from Fall Creek Farm and Nursery's Bushel and Berry collection, bred for a dense, rounded, boxwood-like habit with small, glossy, evergreen-in-mild-climates foliage that holds its shape and color year-round, making it as much a formal hedge or edging plant as a fruit crop. It is self-pollinating, so a single plant will produce a crop of deep-blue, nearly black berries with an intensely aromatic, wild-blueberry-style flavor, though a second nearby blueberry cultivar can improve fruit set. Grow in an acidic, well-drained mix in a container or raised bed, and water consistently since its compact root system dries out faster than a full-sized bush.
sources: Fall Creek Farm and Nursery — Bushel and Berry Collection
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Blueberry Gardener's Guide

common_name: Sapphire Cascade Blueberry (Trailing Self-Fertile Hanging-Basket Blueberry, 'FC12-029')

planting.note: Plant year-round from containers or hanging baskets in mild Gulf Coast winters, or during dormancy elsewhere, into acidic, well-drained potting mix; low chill requirement of roughly 350 hours, well suited to warm Gulf Coast winters.

directions: Sapphire Cascade is a patented Bushel and Berry introduction bred specifically for hanging baskets, with branches that arch outward and trail downward rather than growing upright like a typical blueberry bush. It is self-fertile and produces a classic sweet-tart blueberry flavor on medium-sized berries in early to midsummer, with deciduous foliage that takes on red tones in new growth and again in autumn. Grow in an acidic, well-drained mix in a basket or wide container, and water more frequently than an in-ground planting since hanging baskets dry out quickly in Gulf Coast summer heat.
sources: Fall Creek Farm and Nursery — Bushel and Berry Collection
US Plant Patent USPP32,183

common_name: Midnight Cascade Blueberry (Trailing Vanilla-Flavored Hanging-Basket Blueberry, 'FC12-187')

planting.note: Plant year-round from containers or hanging baskets in mild Gulf Coast winters, or during dormancy elsewhere, into acidic, well-drained potting mix; low chill requirement of roughly 350 hours, well suited to warm Gulf Coast winters.

directions: Midnight Cascade is a patented Bushel and Berry companion to Sapphire Cascade, sharing the same trailing, downward-arching habit bred for hanging baskets rather than a traditional upright bush form. Its deep-blue, medium-sized berries ripen in midsummer with a distinctive hint of vanilla in the flavor, setting it apart from most other blueberry cultivars. It is self-fertile and bears a crop on its own, though pairing it with Sapphire Cascade or another low-chill blueberry nearby can improve pollination and yield.
sources: Fall Creek Farm and Nursery — Bushel and Berry Collection
US Plant Patent USPP32,185
